title: Elder Readiness
subtitle: An honest look at your life against the marks the New Testament sets for an overseer.
intro:
This is not an exam you sit in order to qualify. It is a mirror you hold up before God, alone, with the books of First Timothy, Titus, and First Peter open beside you. The office of elder is not a reward for the gifted or a platform for the eager. It is a weight laid on people whose character has already proven itself in the ordinary rooms of their life, long before anyone asked them to lead.

Answer as you actually are, not as you hope to be seen. No one is reading this but you and the God who already knows. The point is not to pass. The point is to see clearly what is here and what is not yet, so that you can pray honestly and let the people who know you best speak the truth into it.

questions.text: My private life and my public reputation tell the same story, and I would not be ashamed if the two were laid side by side.
I am not a recent convert, and the years have tested my faith rather than merely decorated it.
When I am wronged, I do not nurse it or repay it, and people who have hurt me would say I treated them gently.
My household, whether spouse, children, or those nearest me, would describe me as patient and present rather than harsh or absent.
I can teach the faith plainly and refute error without crushing the person who holds it.
I am self-controlled with money, and no one could fairly call me greedy or driven by gain.
I am hospitable, and my home and table are open to people who can do nothing for me in return.
I do not need to be in charge, and I can submit to other leaders without resentment when I disagree.
Those outside the church who know me would speak well of my integrity even though they do not share my faith.
I am not quick-tempered, and the people who live with me are not careful around my moods.
I am sober and clear-headed, not given to any habit that quietly governs me.
I would shepherd people because I love them, not because I want the standing or the influence the office carries.
I hold firmly to sound doctrine, and I have done the slow work of actually knowing what I believe and why.
I am willing to be examined by others, and I do not flinch when someone names a fault in me.

bands.label: Not yet, and that is not a failure
bands.body:
The honest reading is that the marks are not here yet, and pretending otherwise would help no one. This is not a verdict on your worth or your salvation. It is a word about timing and formation. The New Testament treats eldership as the fruit of a life already proven, not a goal you reach for and then grow into afterward.

Do not let this discourage you into hiding. Let it send you toward the slow work that no shortcut replaces. Sit under faithful teaching. Serve where no one is watching. Let your temper, your money, your household, and your reputation be shaped over years rather than weeks.

The men Paul describes did not become qualified by wanting it badly. They became qualified by being faithful in the small rooms until the character was simply there. That work is in front of you, and it is good work. Walk it without rushing.

bands.label: Something is forming, but it is uneven
bands.body:
There is real evidence of God at work in you, and there are also places that are not ready to carry weight. That mixture is honest, and it is where most people genuinely live. The danger here is not despair. The danger is grabbing the office before the uneven places are tended.

Look hard at the lowest answers you gave. A short temper at home, a quiet hold money has on you, a thin grasp of doctrine, a reputation that wobbles outside the church walls. These are not disqualifications forever. They are the exact places the Spirit is asking you to bring into the light now, before any title makes them harder to face.

Name them to someone who loves you enough to tell you the truth. Let them watch you over time. Character that is only half-proven is not ready to be tested in public, and the people you would lead deserve better than to learn your weaknesses after you already hold the staff.

bands.label: The marks are largely here, but keep listening
bands.body:
Much of what the New Testament asks for appears to be present in you, tested over time and visible to others. That is a serious thing, and it should make you sober rather than satisfied. The closer a person gets to this office, the more carefully they should examine the corners they would rather not look at.

Pay attention to the one or two answers that came back lower than the rest. They are not noise. They are the places that will be exposed under pressure, and the eldership is nothing if not pressure. Do not paper over them because the overall picture looks strong.

This is the moment to invite examination rather than avoid it. Ask the people who live with you, work with you, and worship beside you to speak plainly. A calling confirmed by a watching body is steady. A calling a person confirms alone is fragile, no matter how strong it feels from the inside.

bands.label: The marks are here, let the church confirm it
bands.body:
By your own honest reckoning, the character the New Testament describes has taken root and shown itself over time. That is not a small thing, and it is not something to announce loudly. It is something to carry quietly toward the people God has put around you.

A web page cannot ordain you, and neither can your own confidence. The Spirit works through a local body that has watched your life and can say, with their own mouths, that they see Christ in you. Take this result to your elders, your pastor, and the people closest to you, and ask them to test it honestly, including the places you suspect are weaker than they look.

If the marks are truly here, the confirmation will come, and it will come without your forcing it. Submit to that process. The same humility that makes a man fit to lead is the humility that lets the church, not the candidate, speak the final word.

closing: This is a mirror for discernment before God, and only the local body that knows your life can confirm a calling. A web tool never can.
